newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A prosecution witness has told a provincial court that Sangchai Sunthornvut, the murdered chief of the Mass Communication Organisation of Thailand (MCOT), had told him on three occasions that a former member of the MCOT board wanted him killed. The former MCOT board member named under oath by the witness was widely mentioned in press reports following the murder as possibly being involved. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has distanced himself from the coalition bloc, saying that political parties should not be polarised into two camps. Government and opposition parties have already formed their "alliances", led by the New Aspiration and Democrat parties, favourites to win the most seats in next month's general election. (THE NATION)

- Police have smashed a telephone tampering racket in which criminals tuned mobile handsets to the same frequencies as legal holders in order to get free calls. Four Thais and a Pakistani have been arrested in separate raids and charged. (BANGKOK POST)

- Nithipat Capital Plc has proposed a plan to merge with Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) in the hope of gaining full control of BBC's rehabilitation and management after the bank welcomes new shareholders. The merger plan has been interpreted as the group's trump card to win the authorities' approval to restore BBC now that the central bank has been approached by three more groups -- two from overseas -- for the restoration. (KRUNG THEP THURAKIJ)

- The National Energy Policy Council is expected today to approve a proposal to reduce the Petroleum Authority of Thailand's (PTT) monopoly on fuel oil sales to the state power utility's new power plants, to 50 percent of the total fuel oil required. (THE NATION)
